What the imagery shows

The parts of a roof that are hard to see from the ground.

Each inspection is tied to a question: a suspected defect, a maintenance review or a record of roof condition.

Roof coverings
Junctions and upstands
Drainage
Hard-to-reach areas
01 / 04

What you receive

Visual evidence for the next maintenance decision.

The imagery is tied to the roof areas and details you need to see, so it can feed a practical next step.

Agreed coverage

We confirm the roof areas and details that need to be visible before the flight.

Detailed photographs

Clear aerial photographs of those areas, including parts that are awkward to reach.

Clear handover

The files, with a note of what was captured and anything outstanding.

A basis for what is next

Use the images for maintenance planning, contractor briefing or a specialist survey.

Drone imagery is a visual record. It supports, rather than replaces, a specialist roofing or structural assessment where one is needed.

Suitable briefs

Commercial and residential roofs.

We inspect both. The approach is the same: agree what must be seen, then capture it.

Commercial

Large, complex and multi-building roofs

Big roof areas, plant and multi-building sites. We currently support roof maintenance across a campus of more than 100 buildings for a Cheshire pharmaceutical client.

Discuss a commercial roof →
Residential

Houses and smaller buildings

Pitched and flat roofs seen from above, so you can see the whole roof before deciding on repairs.

Discuss a home roof →

How an inspection runs

Agree it, fly it, check it, hand it over.

The same sequence on every roof, whatever the size.

  1. 01

    Brief

    The roof, the question and any areas of concern.

  2. 02

    Fly

    Capture the agreed areas methodically.

  3. 03

    Check

    Confirm the required areas have been covered.

  4. 04

    Deliver

    Hand over the files and anything outstanding.

Practical questions

Roof inspection questions, answered.

If you know the roof and the question, that is enough to start.

Detailed photographs of the roof areas agreed beforehand, handed over with a clear note of what was captured and anything still outstanding.

No. It gives you clear visual evidence and can reduce the need for close access, but where a specialist roofing, structural or engineering assessment is needed, the imagery supports that work rather than replacing it.

Yes, both. Tell us the property type, the location and what you need to understand when you request a quote.

The roof’s location, the type of property, any areas of concern and how you plan to use the images. You do not need to choose a technical method first.
